_note: Per-city enrichment surfaced as a 'Local context' block on /{intent}-{city}/ pages. Data is factual (postcodes, neighbourhoods, dominant housing era). Missing city = block silently skipped.

london.houseTypes: Victorian and Edwardian terraces dominate inner boroughs, alongside interwar semis in outer London, 1960s-70s tower blocks, and modern glass-fronted apartments in redevelopment zones like Nine Elms and King's Cross.
london.conservationNote: London has over 1,000 conservation areas across 33 boroughs - always check with the local council planning portal before ordering.
london.dominantEra: Victorian to Edwardian across inner London, interwar in outer boroughs.

birmingham.houseTypes: Red-brick Victorian back-to-backs and terraces in inner wards, extensive 1930s semis in outer suburbs, and Brutalist 1960s tower blocks across the city centre.
birmingham.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas across the city, including Bournville and Edgbaston - listed building consent is common in central and inner suburbs.
birmingham.dominantEra: Late Victorian to interwar, with heavy postwar rebuild in the centre.

manchester.houseTypes: Two-up-two-down terraces in inner districts (Hulme, Rusholme, Chorlton), Victorian merchants' villas in Didsbury and Whalley Range, and a wave of modern city-centre apartments post-2000.
manchester.conservationNote: Around 39 conservation areas including Didsbury Village and Victoria Park - sash restoration is common in listed streets.
manchester.dominantEra: Late Victorian terraces predominate; substantial city-centre new-build since 2000.

leeds.houseTypes: Distinctive back-to-back terraces (unique to Leeds and Bradford) in Harehills and Beeston, gritstone Victorian villas in Headingley and Roundhay, plus interwar semis in outer suburbs.
leeds.conservationNote: 48 conservation areas, with strong protection around Headingley, Roundhay Park and the city centre.
leeds.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian, with unique back-to-back stock still lived in.

glasgow.houseTypes: Sandstone tenement flats define the West End and Southside (three or four storeys, high ceilings), interwar semis in Cardonald and Bearsden, and postwar tower blocks across Easterhouse and Drumchapel.
glasgow.conservationNote: 23 conservation areas including Glasgow West and Pollokshields - many tenement blocks are B-listed, restricting frame changes.
glasgow.dominantEra: Late Victorian sandstone tenement stock dominates central and west Glasgow.

liverpool.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around the cathedral and Rodney Street, Victorian terraces across Anfield and Toxteth, and extensive Wavertree/Aigburth interwar semis.
liverpool.conservationNote: 35 conservation areas including Canning, Rodney Street and Woolton village - Georgian glazing bars often need to be replicated.
liverpool.dominantEra: Georgian core surrounded by Victorian and Edwardian suburbs.

bristol.houseTypes: Georgian Clifton townhouses and terraces, Victorian bay-fronts across Bedminster and Southville, plus extensive 1930s semis in Henleaze and Westbury.
bristol.conservationNote: 34 conservation areas - Clifton, Kingsdown and Cliftonwood are especially strict on street-facing frames.
bristol.dominantEra: Georgian Clifton, Victorian across most other neighbourhoods.

sheffield.houseTypes: Stone-built Victorian terraces across Walkley and Nether Edge, red-brick 1930s semis in Dore and Totley, plus 1960s modernist blocks like Park Hill.
sheffield.conservationNote: 38 conservation areas, mostly around south-west suburbs and the Porter Valley.
sheffield.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian stone terraces, interwar semis further out.

edinburgh.houseTypes: Georgian New Town townhouses (heavily A-listed), Victorian tenement flats across Marchmont and Bruntsfield, plus 1930s bungalows in Corstorphine.
edinburgh.conservationNote: The New Town and Old Town are a UNESCO World Heritage Site - any street-facing window change usually requires Listed Building Consent.
edinburgh.dominantEra: Georgian New Town, Victorian tenements everywhere else.

leicester.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around Highfields and Clarendon Park, interwar semis in Knighton and Oadby, plus modern estates on the outer ring.
leicester.conservationNote: 23 conservation areas including Clarendon Park and Stoneygate.

coventry.houseTypes: The city centre was largely rebuilt in the 1950s after WWII bombing, giving Coventry an unusual mix of postwar modernist blocks alongside surviving Victorian terraces in Earlsdon and interwar semis in Chapelfields.
coventry.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas, mostly around surviving prewar suburbs.
coventry.dominantEra: Postwar rebuild in the centre, interwar and Victorian in the suburbs.

bradford.houseTypes: Yorkshire stone back-to-back terraces (shared with Leeds), Victorian mill-owner villas around Manningham, and interwar semis across Wibsey and Idle.
bradford.conservationNote: Saltaire is a UNESCO World Heritage Site - the whole village is a conservation area with strict frame rules.
bradford.dominantEra: Victorian stone terraces, plus interwar suburban growth.

nottingham.houseTypes: The Park Estate is a rare private Victorian villa enclave, surrounded by red-brick terraces in Sneinton and Radford, and interwar semis in West Bridgford and Wollaton.
nottingham.conservationNote: 27 conservation areas including The Park and Lace Market.
nottingham.dominantEra: Victorian to Edwardian, with strong interwar suburban belts.

kingston-upon-hull.houseTypes: Terraced streets off the Avenues in west Hull, interwar Bilton Grange semis, and postwar estates in Bransholme.
kingston-upon-hull.conservationNote: 27 conservation areas including the Avenues and the Old Town.
kingston-upon-hull.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian, with substantial postwar rebuild after WWII bombing.

stoke-on-trent.houseTypes: Federated from six former Potteries towns, so the housing stock is fragmented: pottery workers' terraces in Burslem and Longton, Edwardian villas in Penkhull, and interwar estates in Trentham.
stoke-on-trent.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas, mostly protecting surviving pottery-era terraces.
stoke-on-trent.dominantEra: Late Victorian potters' cottages and terraces.

wolverhampton.houseTypes: Red-brick Victorian terraces around Whitmore Reans and Blakenhall, interwar semis in Tettenhall and Merry Hill, plus a strong interwar municipal housing stock.
wolverhampton.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Tettenhall Wood and Chapel Ash.

plymouth.houseTypes: Devonport and Stonehouse retain Georgian and Victorian stock, but much of central Plymouth was rebuilt after WWII bombing, giving a distinctive Beaux-Arts postwar plan by Patrick Abercrombie.
plymouth.conservationNote: 23 conservation areas including the Barbican and Stonehouse.
plymouth.dominantEra: Postwar centre, Victorian around the Barbican and Devonport.

southampton.houseTypes: Victorian terraces in Portswood and Bevois Valley, interwar semis in Highfield and Bassett, plus dockside modern developments post-2005.
southampton.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Old Town and Bassett Green.
southampton.dominantEra: Victorian to interwar, plus WWII-era rebuild near the docks.

reading.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around Newtown and Katesgrove, interwar semis in Caversham and Tilehurst, plus 1990s-2000s apartments along the Thames and Kennet.
reading.conservationNote: 13 conservation areas including Caversham and central Reading.
reading.dominantEra: Victorian and interwar, with recent riverside new-build.

derby.houseTypes: Terraced streets around Normanton and Pear Tree, interwar semis in Allestree and Chaddesden, plus a growing city-centre apartment stock.
derby.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas, mainly in the historic centre and Little Chester.

newcastle-upon-tyne.houseTypes: Tyneside flats (paired ground and first-floor entrances) in Heaton and Byker, Georgian terraces around Grainger Town, plus 1930s Gosforth semis.
newcastle-upon-tyne.conservationNote: 18 conservation areas including Grainger Town and Jesmond, both with tight frame rules.
newcastle-upon-tyne.dominantEra: Victorian Tyneside flats and Georgian core.

sunderland.houseTypes: Coastal Victorian terraces around Roker and Hendon, Tyneside flats in the western wards, plus 1950s Farringdon and Silksworth estates.
sunderland.conservationNote: 18 conservation areas including Ashbrooke and Roker.
sunderland.dominantEra: Victorian coastal terraces and postwar municipal housing.

aberdeen.houseTypes: Distinctive silver granite Victorian tenements and terraces (Rubislaw quarry stone) - Aberdeen is often called the Granite City for a reason. Interwar bungalows in Cults and Milltimber.
aberdeen.conservationNote: 12 conservation areas including West End and Old Aberdeen - granite frontages carry strict alteration rules.

portsmouth.houseTypes: Terraced streets across Southsea and Fratton, Victorian villas in Old Portsmouth, plus postwar rebuild in the docks area after heavy WWII bombing.
portsmouth.conservationNote: 23 conservation areas including Old Portsmouth and Southsea.
portsmouth.dominantEra: Victorian to Edwardian, plus significant postwar reconstruction.

york.houseTypes: Georgian and early Victorian townhouses within the walls, Victorian brick terraces across Bishophill and The Groves, plus interwar semis in Acomb and Fulford.
york.conservationNote: The historic core is a UNESCO-nominated conservation area - almost any change to street-visible glazing needs Listed Building Consent or approval from City of York Council.
york.dominantEra: Georgian and Victorian in the walled city.

oxford.houseTypes: Golden Cotswold-stone Georgian and Victorian townhouses around Jericho and North Oxford, plus Victorian terraces in East Oxford and Cowley.
oxford.conservationNote: 17 conservation areas covering nearly all of central and North Oxford - single-glazed slim units are often the only permitted upgrade in college-owned streets.
oxford.dominantEra: Georgian and high Victorian, plus interwar in Cowley and Headington.

cambridge.houseTypes: Georgian and Victorian townhouses around the colleges, terraces in Romsey and Petersfield, plus interwar semis in Chesterton and Cherry Hinton.
cambridge.conservationNote: The Central Conservation Area covers most of the college estate - slim double glazing is usually the ceiling for approvals.
cambridge.dominantEra: Georgian core, Victorian and Edwardian belts, interwar suburban growth.

swansea.houseTypes: Terraced streets across Sandfields and Uplands, interwar semis in Sketty and Killay, plus coastal 1960s-70s stock along the Mumbles road.
swansea.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas across Swansea Bay including Uplands and Mumbles.
swansea.dominantEra: Victorian terraces and interwar suburban expansion.

cardiff.houseTypes: Cardiff's signature bay-fronted Victorian terraces dominate Cathays, Roath and Grangetown, with detached Edwardian villas in Cyncoed and Lisvane, and modern apartments in the Bay redevelopment.
cardiff.conservationNote: Around 27 conservation areas including Pontcanna, Roath Park and Cathays Park.

norwich.houseTypes: Medieval and Georgian houses in the walled centre, Victorian terraces across Golden Triangle and Lakenham, plus interwar Eaton Park semis.
norwich.conservationNote: The city centre is a large conservation area - listed building density is one of the highest in England outside London.
norwich.dominantEra: Medieval to Victorian in the walled area, interwar in suburbs.

ipswich.houseTypes: Timber-framed medieval houses around the Ancient House area, Victorian terraces in Wellington Street, plus extensive interwar and postwar suburban housing.
ipswich.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas mostly in the historic centre.
ipswich.dominantEra: Victorian to interwar, with a medieval historic core.

luton.houseTypes: Victorian and Edwardian terraces around the town centre, interwar semis in Stopsley and Round Green, plus postwar Vauxhall factory workers' estates.
luton.conservationNote: Around 7 conservation areas including Wardown Park.

exeter.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around Southernhay, Regency and Victorian villas in St Leonards, plus interwar semis in Pinhoe and Heavitree.
exeter.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas, tight rules around the Cathedral quarter and Southernhay.
exeter.dominantEra: Georgian to Victorian in the centre, interwar in suburbs.

middlesbrough.houseTypes: Terraced streets across central and North Ormesby, interwar semis in Linthorpe and Acklam, plus postwar Whinney Banks and Berwick Hills estates.
middlesbrough.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including Linthorpe and Marton West.
middlesbrough.dominantEra: Late Victorian terraces plus heavy interwar and postwar suburban growth.

peterborough.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around Millfield and Fletton, plus New Town-era estates in Bretton, Orton and Werrington built as designated growth areas from the 1970s.
peterborough.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including the Cathedral Precincts and Longthorpe.
peterborough.dominantEra: Victorian core with major postwar and 1970s New Town growth.

milton-keynes.houseTypes: Founded as a New Town in 1967, MK is almost entirely postwar - Californian-style grid estates, cul-de-sacs and 1980s brick semis. Few conservation-era streets.
milton-keynes.conservationNote: 9 conservation areas focused on the pre-New Town villages of Stony Stratford, Newport Pagnell and Woburn Sands.

northampton.houseTypes: Victorian shoe-worker terraces in Semilong and St James, Edwardian villas in Abington and Kingsley, plus large postwar estates on the edges.
northampton.conservationNote: Around 22 conservation areas including Boot and Shoe Quarter and Abington.
northampton.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian, plus significant postwar overspill housing.

dundee.houseTypes: Distinctive sandstone tenement flats in Broughty Ferry and West End, jute-worker terraces in Lochee and Hilltown, plus 1960s multi-storey blocks in Menzieshill.
dundee.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Broughty Ferry and the West End.
dundee.dominantEra: Victorian sandstone tenements and jute-era terraces.

swindon.houseTypes: The GWR-built New Town cottages in Railway Village (a preserved 1840s workers' estate), Victorian and Edwardian streets in Old Town, plus vast postwar and 1990s estates like West Swindon and Priory Vale.
swindon.conservationNote: 22 conservation areas including the Railway Village, all listed Grade II.
swindon.dominantEra: Victorian railway-era plus dominant postwar expansion.

colchester.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around the Dutch Quarter, Victorian terraces in the New Town, plus interwar and postwar garrison-town semis.
colchester.conservationNote: 26 conservation areas including the Dutch Quarter and Roman Wall.
colchester.dominantEra: Georgian to Victorian core, interwar suburban belts.

chelmsford.houseTypes: Victorian and Edwardian terraces around Moulsham, interwar Marconi-era semis, plus large postwar and 2000s new-builds in Beaulieu Park and Chancellor Park.
chelmsford.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Chelmsford Cathedral and Moulsham Street.
chelmsford.dominantEra: Edwardian and interwar, with recent new-build growth.

southend-on-sea.houseTypes: Seaside Victorian and Edwardian villas along the seafront and Prittlewell, interwar semis in Westcliff and Leigh, plus 1930s-40s bungalow estates common on the Essex coast.
southend-on-sea.conservationNote: Around 18 conservation areas including Old Leigh and Clifftown.

brighton.houseTypes: Regency squares and townhouses around Kemptown, Brunswick and Montpelier - some of the finest Regency architecture in England - plus Victorian terraces in Hanover and Preston.
brighton.conservationNote: 34 conservation areas covering most of Brighton and Hove - Regency frontages carry very strict listed building consent.

bournemouth.houseTypes: Victorian villas around Westbourne and the West Cliff, Edwardian bay-fronts in Winton and Boscombe, plus a distinctive interwar bungalow belt along the seafront.
bournemouth.conservationNote: Around 18 conservation areas including West Cliff and East Overcliff.
bournemouth.dominantEra: Late Victorian to interwar coastal resort.

gloucester.houseTypes: Georgian and Victorian townhouses around the cathedral and dock, terraced streets in Barton and Tredworth, plus interwar semis in Longlevens and Hucclecote.
gloucester.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas across the historic centre and dock quarter.
gloucester.dominantEra: Georgian to Victorian centre, interwar suburbs.

cheltenham.houseTypes: Regency stucco-fronted terraces around Montpellier and Pittville, Victorian villas in Tivoli and The Park, plus interwar semis in Prestbury and Charlton Kings.
cheltenham.conservationNote: The whole central area is a conservation area, with strict rules on stucco frontages and Regency proportions.
cheltenham.dominantEra: Regency spa town, Victorian and Edwardian growth.

blackpool.houseTypes: Terraced streets across central Blackpool, distinctive small B&B and hotel stock, plus interwar semis in Bispham and Stanley Park.
blackpool.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas, several protecting Victorian promenade features.
blackpool.dominantEra: Late Victorian seaside resort, interwar suburban growth.

warrington.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around Bewsey and Latchford, interwar semis in Grappenhall and Stockton Heath, plus the New Town-era Padgate and Birchwood estates.
warrington.conservationNote: Around 25 conservation areas including Stockton Heath and Lymm village.
warrington.dominantEra: Victorian and interwar, plus New Town expansion.

telford.houseTypes: Designated a New Town in 1968 amalgamating existing settlements, so mostly 1970s-1980s brick estates around Dawley, Madeley and Wellington, with historic Ironbridge nearby.
telford.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas mostly in the pre-New Town village cores.
telford.dominantEra: Late Victorian villages plus 1970s New Town.

worcester.houseTypes: Timber-framed medieval houses on Friar Street, Georgian and Regency terraces around the cathedral, plus interwar semis in Warndon and St Peter's.
worcester.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Cathedral Close and Friar Street.
worcester.dominantEra: Medieval to Georgian in the centre, Victorian and interwar around it.

bath.houseTypes: Bath is essentially a Georgian city - Bath stone crescents, terraces and townhouses dominate the centre (Royal Crescent, The Circus, Great Pulteney Street), with Victorian villas in Bathwick and Widcombe.
bath.conservationNote: The centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site - any street-facing window change on a Georgian frontage almost certainly requires Listed Building Consent.

lincoln.houseTypes: Steeply terraced Victorian streets rising up to the cathedral (Steep Hill and around), plus interwar semis on the flatter west and north edges.
lincoln.conservationNote: 17 conservation areas including the Cathedral Quarter and Historic Uphill.
lincoln.dominantEra: Victorian, with a medieval core around the cathedral.

hartlepool.houseTypes: Coastal Victorian terraces around the Headland, interwar semis in Elwick and Grange, plus 1930s and postwar municipal housing in West and Rift House.
hartlepool.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including the Headland and Seaton Carew.

blackburn.houseTypes: Cotton-mill terraces across most inner wards, some Victorian villas around Corporation Park, plus 1930s and postwar semis on the outer belt.
blackburn.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas including Corporation Park and Preston New Road.

huddersfield.houseTypes: Yorkshire stone terraces across Marsh and Longwood, Victorian mill-owner villas around Edgerton, plus interwar semis in Almondbury.
huddersfield.conservationNote: 42 conservation areas across Kirklees, many in Huddersfield's mill-era neighbourhoods.

poole.houseTypes: Georgian and early Victorian houses in the Old Town, Victorian villas in Parkstone, plus extensive interwar Sandbanks-adjacent stock and 1960s tower blocks around the harbour.
poole.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Old Town Poole and Canford Cliffs.

eastbourne.houseTypes: Elegant Victorian and Edwardian seafront terraces (Devonshire Park, Meads), plus interwar Willingdon and Hampden Park estates.
eastbourne.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including Devonshire Place and Meads.

hastings.houseTypes: Fisherman's Old Town cottages, Victorian and Edwardian terraces up the West Hill, plus 1960s tower blocks on the seafront.
hastings.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Old Town and Burton St Leonards.
hastings.dominantEra: Georgian Old Town and Regency St Leonards, with Victorian expansion.

maidstone.houseTypes: Kent ragstone Georgian and Victorian townhouses around the town centre, plus interwar semis in Loose and Barming.
maidstone.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas across the borough including Loose village and central Maidstone.

basildon.houseTypes: Designated a New Town in 1949 and largely built between 1955 and 1975 - 1960s brick semis, low-rise flat blocks and pedestrianised estates dominate. Little pre-war stock.
basildon.conservationNote: Around 5 conservation areas mostly in pre-New Town villages like Vange and Laindon.

shrewsbury.houseTypes: Timber-framed Tudor and Georgian townhouses within the medieval loop of the River Severn, Victorian villas in Belle Vue, plus interwar and modern estates around Radbrook and Bicton Heath.
shrewsbury.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including the medieval town centre - many buildings are Grade I or II listed.

guildford.houseTypes: Cobbled Georgian and Victorian High Street houses, Edwardian villas along Epsom Road and London Road, plus interwar and 1990s semis in Merrow and Burpham.
guildford.conservationNote: Around 25 conservation areas including the town centre.
guildford.dominantEra: Georgian to Edwardian core, interwar suburbs.

slough.houseTypes: Terraced streets around Chalvey and Cippenham, extensive 1930s Britwell and Manor Park semis, plus postwar tower blocks and modern town-centre apartments.
slough.conservationNote: Around 6 conservation areas mostly around older pre-industrial pockets.

st-albans.houseTypes: Medieval and Georgian houses around the cathedral and Fishpool Street, Victorian and Edwardian villas in Marshalswick and Marlborough Road, plus interwar semis in Bricket Wood.
st-albans.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including the Cathedral Quarter and Verulamium.

woking.houseTypes: Late Victorian and Edwardian villas around the town centre, interwar Sheerwater and Byfleet semis, plus postwar and modern estates in Goldsworth Park and Kingfield.
woking.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Horsell and Old Woking.
woking.dominantEra: Late Victorian to interwar suburban town.

wigan.houseTypes: Cotton and coal-era Victorian terraces across Whelley and Springfield, interwar semis in Standish and Orrell, plus postwar municipal estates in Marsh Green.
wigan.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including Standish and Wigan Pier.

bolton.houseTypes: Cotton-mill Victorian terraces across Halliwell and Great Lever, Victorian villas around Chorley New Road, plus interwar semis in Astley Bridge and Breightmet.
bolton.conservationNote: 24 conservation areas including Chorley New Road and Bradshaw.

bury.houseTypes: Victorian mill-worker terraces around the town centre, interwar semis in Whitefield and Prestwich, plus 1970s and 1980s estates in Radcliffe.
bury.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Ramsbottom and Prestwich village.

salford.houseTypes: Terraces of Coronation Street style predominate in Weaste and Ordsall (many now demolished), plus Victorian villas in Broughton and modern MediaCity apartments.
salford.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Worsley and Broughton.
salford.dominantEra: Late Victorian terraces plus major modern regeneration.

stockport.houseTypes: Victorian mill terraces near the viaduct, Edwardian bay-fronted villas in Heaton Moor and Davenport, plus interwar semis in Bramhall and Cheadle.
stockport.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas including Marple and Heaton Moor.
stockport.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian, interwar suburban belt.

rochdale.houseTypes: Cotton-mill Victorian terraces (Rochdale is a birthplace of the co-operative movement), Victorian villas in Norden and Bamford, plus interwar and postwar semis further out.
rochdale.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Rochdale town centre and Littleborough.

oldham.houseTypes: Cotton-mill Victorian terraces across central Oldham, Victorian villas in Werneth and Waterhead, plus 1930s semis in Chadderton and Royton.
oldham.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Saddleworth villages (Uppermill, Delph, Dobcross).

burnley.houseTypes: Distinctive stone-built Victorian terraces (mostly two-up-two-downs), some Victorian villas in Padiham Road, plus interwar semis in Reedley and Rose Grove.
burnley.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including Burnley Wood and Padiham.

durham.houseTypes: Georgian and early Victorian townhouses on the peninsula around the cathedral, Victorian pit-village terraces in the outer areas, plus interwar suburban semis.
durham.conservationNote: The Cathedral peninsula is a UNESCO World Heritage Site; around 20 conservation areas in total.

darlington.houseTypes: Railway-era Victorian and Edwardian streets around Northgate, terraces off Yarm Road, plus interwar semis in West Auckland Road and Blackwell.
darlington.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Blackwell and Cockerton.

stockton-on-tees.houseTypes: Georgian High Street and Riverside terraces, Victorian streets around Norton, plus large interwar and postwar suburban housing across Ingleby Barwick and Fairfield.
stockton-on-tees.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including Yarm and Norton.
stockton-on-tees.dominantEra: Georgian and Victorian core plus interwar suburban growth.

wakefield.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around the city centre, Edwardian villas in St John's, plus interwar semis in Sandal and Lupset.
wakefield.conservationNote: 40+ conservation areas across the district including central Wakefield and Sandal.
wakefield.dominantEra: Victorian and Edwardian core, plus interwar.

doncaster.houseTypes: Victorian and Edwardian streets around Balby and Wheatley, coal-village terraces in Bentley and Edlington, plus extensive interwar semis in Cantley.
doncaster.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas including Doncaster Town Centre and Bawtry.

barnsley.houseTypes: Coal-mining Victorian terraces across the town centre and pit villages (Grimethorpe, Cudworth), interwar Kendray semis, plus postwar municipal housing.
barnsley.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including central Barnsley and Cawthorne.

rotherham.houseTypes: Steel and mining-era Victorian terraces around the town centre and Kimberworth, plus interwar semis in Broom and Sitwell.
rotherham.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including Wentworth village and central Rotherham.

mansfield.houseTypes: Mining-era Victorian terraces, interwar semis in Forest Town and Warsop, plus postwar estates on the outer edges.
mansfield.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including central Mansfield.

chesterfield.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around the town centre (famous for the crooked spire), Edwardian villas in Brampton, plus interwar semis in Boythorpe and Newbold.
chesterfield.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including the town centre with St Mary's spire.

burton-upon-trent.houseTypes: Brewing-era Victorian terraces around Shobnall and Anglesey, Edwardian villas along Ashby Road, plus interwar semis in Winshill and Stapenhill.
burton-upon-trent.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas including Burton Central and Rolleston.

kidderminster.houseTypes: Carpet-industry Victorian terraces around the town centre, Edwardian villas in Hoo Road, plus interwar semis in Blakebrook and Broadwaters.
kidderminster.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including central Kidderminster and Bewdley.

redditch.houseTypes: Designated a New Town in 1964, so mostly 1970s brick semis, terraces and estates around Church Hill, Winyates and Woodrow. Some pre-New Town Victorian and needle-industry stock in Old Redditch.
redditch.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas mostly in pre-New Town villages.

nuneaton.houseTypes: Victorian mining-era terraces in Attleborough and Stockingford, interwar semis in Chapel End, plus large postwar and 1990s estates on the north edge.
nuneaton.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including central Nuneaton.

walsall.houseTypes: Victorian terraces around Palfrey and Chuckery, interwar semis in Streetly and Bloxwich, plus postwar municipal estates on the outer belt.
walsall.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Aldridge and Rushall.

dudley.houseTypes: Victorian ironworker terraces across Dudley and Netherton, interwar semis in Sedgley and Wollaston, plus postwar estates around Russells Hall.
dudley.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Sedgley and Stourbridge.

lichfield.houseTypes: Medieval and Georgian townhouses around the Cathedral Close, Victorian and Edwardian villas along Beacon Street, plus modern estates in Streethay.
lichfield.conservationNote: The Cathedral Close and much of the historic centre is a conservation area with tight rules.

tamworth.houseTypes: Historic core around the Castle and Church Street, but the majority of housing stock is postwar overspill from Birmingham (1960s-70s estates in Wilnecote and Amington).
tamworth.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas including the Castle and Church Street.

stafford.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around the market square, Victorian and Edwardian villas along Newport Road, plus interwar and postwar semis in Baswich and Rising Brook.
stafford.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including central Stafford and Milford.
stafford.dominantEra: Georgian to Victorian core, plus interwar.

leamington-spa.houseTypes: Regency stucco terraces around the Parade and Clarendon Square (one of the best-preserved Regency spa towns), Victorian villas in Lillington, plus interwar semis in Sydenham.
leamington-spa.conservationNote: The Regency core is a conservation area with the strictest rules in Warwickshire - stucco frontages need Listed Building Consent.

warwick.houseTypes: Medieval Warwick Castle and Tudor timber-framed houses on Mill Street, Georgian rebuild after the 1694 town fire, plus Victorian villas in West Rock and interwar semis in Woodloes Park.
warwick.conservationNote: The medieval town centre is a conservation area covering most streets within the old walls.

rugby.houseTypes: Rail and cement-era Victorian streets around the town centre, Edwardian villas near Rugby School, plus interwar semis in Bilton and Hillmorton.
rugby.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas including central Rugby and Rugby School environs.

hereford.houseTypes: Medieval and Georgian townhouses around the Cathedral and Old House, Victorian villas along Aylestone Hill, plus interwar semis in Belmont and Tupsley.
hereford.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including the Cathedral Close and King Street.
hereford.dominantEra: Medieval to Georgian core, Victorian and interwar around.

newport.houseTypes: Coal and steel-era Victorian terraces around Pill and Maindee, Edwardian villas along Christchurch Road, plus interwar semis in Malpas and Bettws.
newport.conservationNote: Around 25 conservation areas across the borough including Caerleon (Roman origin) and central Newport.

wrexham.houseTypes: Coal-mining Victorian terraces around Rhosddu and Rhosllannerchrugog, plus interwar semis in Acton and Coedpoeth.
wrexham.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including central Wrexham and Erddig.

chester.houseTypes: Timber-framed medieval Rows in the walled centre (one of the best-preserved in England), Georgian townhouses around Bridge Street, plus Victorian and Edwardian villas in Hoole and Handbridge.
chester.conservationNote: The whole walled city is a conservation area with UNESCO nomination - listed building consent is routine.

crewe.houseTypes: Railway-industry Victorian terraces around the station (Crewe was created by the LNWR), Edwardian villas around Nantwich Road, plus interwar semis in Wistaston and Willaston.
crewe.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including central Crewe and Nantwich.

loughborough.houseTypes: Hosiery-era Victorian terraces around the town centre and Shepshed Road, Edwardian villas around Nanpantan Road, plus interwar semis in Hathern Road and Thorpe Acre.
loughborough.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including central Loughborough and Quorn.

bedford.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around the Embankment and High Street, Victorian and Edwardian villas in Kimbolton Road, plus interwar semis in Elstow and Kempston.
bedford.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including central Bedford and Elstow.
bedford.dominantEra: Georgian to Victorian core, plus interwar.

grantham.houseTypes: Georgian High Street townhouses, Victorian terraces around Belton Lane, plus interwar semis in Barrowby Gate and Great Gonerby.
grantham.conservationNote: Around 10 conservation areas including central Grantham.

gainsborough.houseTypes: Georgian and Victorian townhouses around the Old Hall, Victorian terraces near the town centre, plus interwar and postwar suburban semis.
gainsborough.conservationNote: Around 5 conservation areas including the Old Hall and central Gainsborough.

scunthorpe.houseTypes: Steel-industry Victorian and Edwardian terraces, extensive interwar Crosby and Old Brumby semis (built for steelworkers), plus postwar estates.
scunthorpe.conservationNote: Around 6 conservation areas including central Scunthorpe.

grimsby.houseTypes: Fishing-industry Victorian terraces around the East and West Marsh, Edwardian villas along Bargate, plus interwar semis in Nunsthorpe and Grange.
grimsby.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including central Grimsby and Cleethorpes.

scarborough.houseTypes: Seaside Victorian and Edwardian villas along the North and South Bays (Regency Crescent, Belvoir Terrace), terraced streets around Falsgrave, plus interwar semis in Newby and Scalby.
scarborough.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including central Scarborough seafront.
scarborough.dominantEra: Late Victorian to Edwardian coastal resort.

harrogate.houseTypes: Elegant Victorian and Edwardian spa-era villas around the Stray, Regency terraces off Montpellier, plus interwar semis in Starbeck and Bilton.
harrogate.conservationNote: Around 20 conservation areas including the Stray and Montpellier - tight rules on stucco and stone frontages.

keighley.houseTypes: Yorkshire stone mill terraces around the town centre and Braithwaite, Victorian villas in Utley and Fell Lane, plus interwar semis in Riddlesden and Long Lee.
keighley.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas across Bradford district including Haworth (Bronte country).

salisbury.houseTypes: Medieval and Georgian houses in the Cathedral Close (Sir Christopher Wren, Constable painting), Victorian terraces around Fisherton Street, plus interwar semis in Bemerton and Harnham.
salisbury.conservationNote: The Cathedral Close is one of the most important conservation areas in southern England - Listed Building Consent is routine.
salisbury.dominantEra: Medieval to Georgian core, Victorian and interwar around.

truro.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around Lemon Street and Walsingham Place, Victorian terraces up Kenwyn Hill, plus modern estates on the north edge.
truro.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas across the district including central Truro and Falmouth.

torquay.houseTypes: Regency and Victorian villas around the seafront (Torquay grew as a Regency resort), terraced streets in Ellacombe and Chelston, plus interwar bungalows in Cockington and St Marychurch.
torquay.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including central Torquay and Cockington village.

taunton.houseTypes: Georgian townhouses around the Crescent and Vivary Park, Victorian villas along Staplegrove Road, plus interwar and postwar semis in Rowbarton and Trull.
taunton.conservationNote: Around 12 conservation areas including central Taunton.

yeovil.houseTypes: Glove-industry Victorian terraces around Kingston, Edwardian villas in Preston Road, plus interwar semis in Larkhill and Milford.
yeovil.conservationNote: Around 8 conservation areas including central Yeovil.

tunbridge-wells.houseTypes: Regency and Victorian villas around the Common and Mount Ephraim, Georgian Pantiles-adjacent terraces, plus interwar and postwar detached houses in Southborough and Rusthall.
tunbridge-wells.conservationNote: Around 25 conservation areas including the Pantiles and Calverley Park.

ashford.houseTypes: Victorian railway-era terraces around New Town, plus large postwar and 2000s estates in Kingsnorth and Repton Park.
ashford.conservationNote: Around 25 conservation areas across the borough including central Ashford and Wye.

folkestone.houseTypes: Regency and Victorian seafront villas around the Leas (a mile-long clifftop promenade), plus terraces in Central Folkestone and interwar semis in Cheriton.
folkestone.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including the Leas and Bayle.

dover.houseTypes: Georgian and Victorian townhouses around the seafront and Castle Hill, terraced streets in the Old Town, plus interwar and postwar semis in Buckland and River.
dover.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including central Dover and St Margaret's.

Canterbury.houseTypes: Medieval and Tudor timber-framed houses in the walled centre (World Heritage Cathedral precinct), Georgian townhouses along the High Street, plus Victorian villas in St Dunstan's and modern estates in Thanington.
Canterbury.conservationNote: The Cathedral precinct is a UNESCO World Heritage Site - Listed Building Consent is routine within the walls.

high-wycombe.houseTypes: Furniture-industry Victorian terraces around the town centre, Edwardian villas in Amersham Hill, plus interwar semis in Booker and Downley and postwar estates in Micklefield.
high-wycombe.conservationNote: Around 30 conservation areas across Buckinghamshire including High Wycombe centre.

stevenage.houseTypes: Designated the first postwar New Town in 1946, so almost entirely postwar - 1950s Bedwell and Broadwater estates, 1960s-70s tower blocks, plus more recent Symonds Green.
stevenage.conservationNote: Around 5 conservation areas including Stevenage Old Town.

crawley.houseTypes: Designated a New Town in 1947, largely 1950s-60s brick semis and low-rise estates in 13 planned neighbourhoods (Northgate, West Green, Ifield). Little pre-war stock.
crawley.conservationNote: Around 6 conservation areas including Crawley High Street and Ifield.

worthing.houseTypes: Regency seaside villas around Steyne Gardens, Victorian terraces in Central Worthing and Broadwater, plus interwar bungalows in Goring and Ferring.
worthing.conservationNote: Around 15 conservation areas including Steyne Gardens and Ambrose Place.

croydon.houseTypes: Victorian and Edwardian bay-fronts across Thornton Heath and South Croydon, interwar semis in Selsdon and Coulsdon, plus 1960s-70s Croydon town centre high-rises.
croydon.conservationNote: Around 24 conservation areas including South End and Park Hill.
croydon.dominantEra: Late Victorian and Edwardian suburbia with heavy 1960s CBD rebuild.
